overview: This file traces U.S. Department of State efforts from 1930 to 1934 to obtain and transmit telephone—and, in 1931, telegraph—statistics for Japanese-administered communications systems in the Kwantung Leased Territory and elsewhere in Manchuria, chiefly for the American Telephone and Telegraph Company. It contains State Department instructions, consular despatches from Dairen, statistical questionnaires comparing conditions in 1929–1931, and cross-reference sheets pointing to later correspondence. The documents record exchanges, telephones, wire mileage, employees, traffic, revenues, investment, population, and city-level development, while repeatedly noting that changing territorial coverage and the unavailability of South Manchuria Railway Zone data complicated comparisons.

people.name: Thomas
people.role: Author of the referenced 1932 despatch from Dairen; full name and position are not stated on the cross-reference sheet

people.name: John Carter Vincent
people.role: U.S. consular officer identified on the 1934 cross-reference sheet only by surname

subfiles.title: Instruction requesting updated Kwantung telephone statistics
subfiles.about: The Department of State requests updated government and private telephone statistics for the Kwantung Leased Territory on behalf of the American Telephone and Telegraph Company.
subfiles.summary: Instruction requests updated 1930 Kwantung telephone statistics, encloses forms and AT&T's world statistics publication, asking for triplicate returns via despatch.

subfiles.title: Despatch from Coville transmitting 1930 telephone statistics
subfiles.from: Cabot Coville, American Vice Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Coville submits the completed telephone questionnaire and explains that its territorial coverage excludes the South Manchuria Railway Zone.
subfiles.summary: Coville transmits AT&T's requested questionnaire, cautioning the 1929 report covered both Kwantung and the Railway Zone while new figures cover only Kwantung, since the Bureau of Communications declined to release zone statistics that year.

subfiles.title: Kwantung telephone statistics for 1929–1930
subfiles.from: Bureau of Communications, Kwantung Government, transmitted by the American Consulate at Dairen
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State and American Telephone and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The enclosure tabulates Japanese government telephone operations and city-level telephone development in the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Table compares 1929-30 Kwantung telephone figures: offices, phones, wire length, employment, calls, revenue, and population, showing growth from 9,580 to 10,732 phones and 83.3 to 96.1 million calls; a second table covers five towns.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to AT&T acknowledgment
subfiles.about: The sheet refers researchers to a letter acknowledging receipt of the telephone statistics sent from Dairen.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to an AT&T letter (893.75/83) thanking the Department for Dairen's transmitted telephone statistics.

subfiles.title: Langdon despatch transmitting the 1931 communications survey
subfiles.from: William R. Langdon, American Consul at Dairen
subfiles.about: Langdon submits a survey of telephone conditions in the Kwantung Leased Territory for transmission to the American Telephone and Telegraph Company.
subfiles.summary: Langdon encloses three copies of the 1931 communications survey, responding to AT&T's May request per the Department's June instruction.

subfiles.title: Kwantung telephone and telegraph statistics for 1930–1931
subfiles.from: American Consulate at Dairen using Japanese government statistics
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of State and American Telephone and Telegraph Company
subfiles.about: The enclosure compares telephone development in 1930 and 1931 and supplies a separate statistical profile of the Japanese government telegraph system.
subfiles.summary: Table shows telephones growing from 10,732 to 11,470 and revenue from ¥1.17 to ¥1.51 million; a city table flags a possible Dairen inconsistency; telegraph table reports 87 offices, 3.17 million messages, ¥874,632 revenue, and 91 employees for 1931.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Thomas despatch on Kwantung statistics
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a separate despatch concerning telephone statistics for the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Thomas's 1932 Dairen despatch no. 18 on Kwantung telephone statistics, filed at 893.75/121.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Vincent despatch on Manchurian statistical coverage
subfiles.about: The sheet points to a despatch explaining the geographic coverage of telephone statistics for the Mukden and Harbin districts.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Vincent's 1934 despatch no. 77: Mukden/Harbin statistics cover Manchuria except the Railway Zone and Kwantung, filed at 893.75/149.

interest: Shows detailed Kwantung telephone/telegraph growth statistics, with consular caution about non-comparable Railway Zone data.
